perspective:
Ethan’s available information:

- He is a long-time close friend of Gary Guo; they met in middle school and have supported each other over the years.
- He knows Gary works long hours at a hospital.
- He personally noticed Gary overworking, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep.
- He invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. He heard Gary initially decline because there was too much to do at the hospital, but they later attended the retreat.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected Gary’s overwork had deeper causes.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school and Gary could tell him anything. Gary replied that it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Gary opened up to Ethan about pressure from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary, discussed Gary’s progress and remaining challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, and felt hopeful and proud. He told Gary he was proud and available to talk.
- Gary told Ethan things were better, he was less overwhelmed, and he had had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- After a year, Ethan observed Gary managing better on his own, felt satisfied and happy, and decided to step back. He told Gary he was always a call away but believed Gary had it. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
